screens.name: Home — settled, transition, successful omen fixture
screens.evidence: Sheets 08–09 show a dominant orb and both omen states; supplied runtime reports reduced-motion coverage; provisional A 8.2, F 7.8, overall 8.0.
findings: Increase the sample question’s prominence and make the orb’s primary-action role more immediately recognizable.

screens.name: Approach — settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 01 preserves readable status beneath the enlarged orb, and supplied runtime specifies automatic advance with an immediate reduced-motion path; provisional A 8.3, F 7.8, overall 8.0.
findings: Verify the brief automatic transition on a physical device with screen-reader announcements enabled.

screens.name: Ask — settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 02 shows stable input and action placement, while supplied runtime reports successful question submission; provisional A 8.2, F 7.8, overall 8.0.
findings: Replace the implementation-oriented prediction-engine explanation with a concise explanation of what happens to the question.

screens.name: Ask — 200% text
screens.evidence: Sheet 01 shows a complete enlarged question, stacked actions and visible submission, with browser enlargement checks reported; provisional A 8.0, F 7.8, overall 7.9.
findings: Verify that the enlarged form retains its context and submission action above a physical phone keyboard.

screens.name: Listening — voice failure, settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 09 elevates typing above voice retry and explains the microphone failure, while runtime reports transcription preservation; provisional A 8.0, F 8.2, overall 8.1.
findings: Place the voice-failure explanation closer to the fallback actions so their purpose is clear before reaching the bottom notice.

screens.name: Planning — loading, settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 11 shows readable stage, timing, credit protection and cancellation copy in both captures; provisional A 8.3, F 8.0, overall 8.1.
findings: Verify that the loading-stage announcement and cancellation control remain discoverable with physical assistive technology.

screens.name: Question 1 — settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 02 shows stable question, progress and answer rows, supported by reported Space/Enter advancement and Back restoration; provisional A 8.5, F 8.0, overall 8.2.
findings: Verify that immediate answer advancement announces the next question clearly on VoiceOver and TalkBack.

screens.name: Question 2 — settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 03 retains the first question’s geometry and advances the labeled progress indicator; provisional A 8.5, F 8.0, overall 8.2.
findings: Confirm with novice use that immediate advancement and Back provide sufficient confidence when an answer is tapped accidentally.

screens.name: Question 3 — settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 03 shows consistent final-question layout with explicit 3-of-3 progress and readable choices; provisional A 8.5, F 8.0, overall 8.2.
findings: Clarify that choosing the final answer starts prediction generation if novice testing finds that transition surprising.

screens.name: Question heading — keyboard focus
screens.evidence: Sheet 01 shows visible heading focus, and supplied keyboard evidence reports focus transfer followed by Tab access to the first answer; provisional A 7.8, F 8.2, overall 8.0.
findings: Give the heading focus outline breathing room and align its treatment with the settings focus indicator.

screens.name: Custom answer — empty, settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 04 shows question context, Your answer, Change and disabled Continue, with text retention reported in runtime evidence; provisional A 8.0, F 7.8, overall 7.9.
findings: Make the empty-input requirement explicit so the low-contrast disabled Continue does not carry that explanation alone.

screens.name: Custom answer — empty at 200%
screens.evidence: Sheet 04 preserves the full enlarged question, input label and Change action while keeping Continue visible; provisional A 8.0, F 7.8, overall 7.9.
findings: Check native text enlargement and keyboard presentation together before accepting the enlarged form’s accessibility.

screens.name: Custom answer — filled at 200%
screens.evidence: Sheet 05 shows a readable multiline answer and fully visible Reveal my prediction button beneath its question; provisional A 8.2, F 8.0, overall 8.1.
findings: Verify longer answers and cursor movement on a physical device without losing the question or submission control.

screens.name: Custom answer — synthetic keyboard-constrained viewport
screens.evidence: Sheet 05 shows readable entered text and submission but no visible question heading and a clipped label fragment, despite reported browser context-retention checks; provisional A 7.5, F 7.3, overall 7.4.
findings: Provide a capture with the question context visible above the constrained input and resolve the clipped label fragment.

screens.name: Research — loading, settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 11–12 retain the loading composition while changing the explanation to current-context research; provisional A 8.3, F 8.0, overall 8.1.
findings: Verify that the changed stage explanation is announced without repeatedly interrupting assistive-technology users.

screens.name: Planning error — settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 06 shows failure explanation, charge protection, prominent retry and question editing in a stable layout; provisional A 8.3, F 8.2, overall 8.2.
findings: Verify that retry failure returns focus to the explanation while preserving the original question.

screens.name: Prediction error — settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 06 adds Review answers to retry and edit recovery, and supplied runtime reports connection recovery; provisional A 8.3, F 8.2, overall 8.2.
findings: Verify native focus order across retry, answer review and question editing after a prediction failure.

screens.name: Reveal — settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 12–13 show a prominent forecast, qualification and share action, with real-flow reveal and sampled entrance contrast reported; provisional A 8.3, F 7.8, overall 8.0.
findings: Group the four secondary actions more tightly by purpose to reduce the competing choices beneath sharing.

screens.name: Reveal — expanded Why, settled and transition

screens.name: Check-in — settled and transition

screens.name: Saved outcome — Not quite

screens.name: Sensitive redirect — planning, settled and transition

screens.name: Sensitive redirect — prediction, settled and transition

components.name: Atmospheric background
components.evidence: Dark mist remains subordinate in the supplied stills, and runtime reports sampled composited contrast, sustained browser performance and stopped draws under reduced motion; provisional A 8.3, F 8.0, overall 8.1.

limitations: All scores are provisional; this evaluation uses only the attached sheets and supplied runtime narrative, without independently rerunning checks.
Corresponding transition captures retain coherent composition and readable text, but paired stills cannot establish complete temporal continuity or absence of intermediate layout shifts.
Reported browser checks support browser behavior only; physical iPhone Safari, native text enlargement, keyboard safe areas, VoiceOver/TalkBack, microphone hardware and haptics remain unverified.
PNG generation and injected export recovery are reported; OS share delivery, real payments and configured social/authentication services are not established.
Synthetic predictions and deliberately labeled fixture copy were assessed for layout only, not production wording, semantic quality or predictive accuracy.
The synthetic keyboard capture visibly lacks the question heading; supplied context-retention checks do not resolve that screenshot-level concern or prove a physically inaccessible control.
No demonstrated hard-gate failure is established by this packet, but unverified boundaries prevent certification that every gate passes.
The authorized A >=9 and F >=9 threshold is not met for any screen or component, and the physical/assistive evidence required for 9/10 certification is absent.
No separate modal is represented; full-screen Plans, Share, Story and recovery states are graded individually.
topFixes: Resolve and recapture the keyboard-constrained custom-answer state with visible question context and no clipped label.
Improve enlarged-text tab labels and verify physical keyboard, screen-reader and touch-target behavior across core actions.
Make expanded explanations easier to scan and reduce the competing secondary actions beneath Reveal.
Compact notices and simplify the offline Circles explanation while preserving explicit recovery and availability status.
Complete physical-device and assistive-technology checks before considering premium-score certification.
